correctness.rationale: The Fourier dispersion h(k)=4−2cos k1−2cos k2 has essential spectrum [0,8]. The exact two-site Birman–Schwinger determinant is 1−λ²(G0−Gr)(G0+Gr). For κ>0 both nonnegative Fourier-integral factors are strictly decreasing to 0; G0−Gr tends to the finite positive lattice resistance Rr, while G0+Gr diverges at κ=0, giving one simple root for every λ>0. The square-lattice Watson elliptic formula yields G0=(4π)^(-1) log(32/κ)+O(κ|logκ|) and G0−Gr=Rr+O(κ|logκ|); hence the exact prefactor and exponent. Reflection in r/2 followed by bipartite sign conjugates H to 8I−H, yielding exactly one upper root. For e1, (4+κ)G0−4G_e1=1 yields R_e1=1/4.
